{{Quote|These particular craft have a capability previously unheard of for ships their size, the ability to evade sensors and scanners, rendering them effectively invisible. Obviously, with a fleet of such vessels, Darth Vader could devastate our forces with near impunity.|Admiral Gial Ackbar|audio=Ackbar-RAII.flac|<ref name="RAII" />}}
The '''TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter''', also referred to as the '''TIE/ph phantom''', '''TIE Phantom''' or '''Phantom V38''', was a prototype [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] developed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. A modified [[V38 assault fighter]], the TIE phantom was the result of a development project led by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Martio Batch]] and was equipped with both [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] and a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], along with a technology not seen for decades&mdash;a [[Stygium/Legends|stygium]] [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]].

The development process began in response to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] victory at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. After some initial troubles, Batch was able to secure a supply of the stygium [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] required by the cloaking device, and the fighters entered production on [[Imdaar Alpha]]. When the testing process was completed following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] intended to use the new starfighter in a devastating assault on the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Alliance Fleet]]. However, over a series of encounters, the Rebels learned of the new threat. Recognizing the danger, the Alliance dispatched [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] [[Rookie One]] and [[Ru Murleen]] to capture one of the fighters for study.

The Rebels successfully infiltrated the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] ''[[Terror]]'' as it prepared to launch the fighters against the Alliance and escaped with one of them, which they used to destroy both the ''Terror'' and the [[Imdaar Alpha research station|facility]] where the fighters were produced. However, the Rebels' acquisition of the fighter was short-lived&mdash;when the stolen TIE phantom's [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]] activated before the Rebels could examine the fighter, the technology was lost. After this, the fighters were kept in limited supply and given only to the most capable of Imperial fighter pilots.

==Characteristics==
===Design===
{{Quote|Scanners are picking up something strange; I can't get a firm fix on anything.|Ru Murleen|audio=Phantom-RAII.flac|<ref name="RAII" />}}
The TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter<ref name="SoT" /> was a modified version of the failed [[V38 assault fighter]],<ref name="SoR">{{FFG|story=Phantoms in the Dark|book=Strongholds of Resistance}}</ref> leading some to refer to the [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] by this designation, as well as the more common "Phantom TIE." It was a member of the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]], which dominated the Empire's starfighter [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. However, it was distinctive among the series in that its [[Solar collector/Legends|solar array]] wings were attached directly to the fuselage, perpendicular to the hull, rather than to pylons extending from it. Like in the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defender]], the wings were equally spaced around the hull, with one located directly above the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]], and two below and to either side.<ref name="RAII" />

Whereas most TIE series starfighters in use at the time had a spherical cockpit section, the TIE phantom's cockpit was elongated,<ref name="RAII" /> and reminiscent of some [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]], including the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]], and the later [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar]] [[Scimitar assault bomber]].<ref name="EGVV">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> The section behind the cockpit was roughly triangular, with the wings mounted to the tips.<ref name="RAII" /> This hull section was heavily armored and contained the [[Starship/Legends|ship's]] [[Twin ion engine/Legends|twin ion engines]], [[Power generator/Legends|power generators]] and stealth systems.<ref name="SoT" /> Starships carrying TIE phantoms had to be fitted with specialized maintenance, launch and recovery systems.<ref name="SoR" /> With no landing gear, the fighters had to be supported when aboard ship to keep the lower wings off the surface. A launch mechanism would grip the fighter by the upper wing and maneuver it into position when departing.<ref name="RAII" />

[[File:TIEPhantom1.png|thumb|left|250px|A TIE phantom with its entry hatch open.]]
Entry into the cockpit was possible through an elevator hatch on the bottom of the fuselage.<ref name="RAII" /> The fighter was designed for a crew of two: one [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] the vessel, while the other acted as a [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] and copilot.<ref name="SoT" /> The crew's positions in the cockpit were staggered, with the gunner sitting forward and to the right, while the pilot took the rear left console. Both positions had a [[Computer/Legends|computer]] display, along with the controls required to operate the ship. Unlike most fighters in the TIE series, the TIE phantom featured [[Life support/Legends|life support]] systems, allowing the crew to operate it without the bulky helmet and breathing equipment required by most [[TIE pilot]]s. The crew did, however, wear a headset with a microphone and headphones to assist communication in-flight.<ref name="RAII" /> In addition to the crew, the fighter had storage space for ninety [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] of cargo.<ref name="RECG" />

===Armament and propulsion===
The TIE phantom was armed with two [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] mounted to the body under the cockpit, which could be set to fire-linked.<ref name="RAII" /> Three more [[Laser/Legends|laser]] cannons were mounted on the tips of its three wings, and all five could be fired simultaneously to maximize the effectiveness of a shot.<ref name="FOC" /> The vessel was designed to be tougher than the ubiquitous [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]], and also possessed [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] for defense&mdash;a feature not present in standard TIE models.<ref name="SoT" />

The fighter had a maximum [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheric]] speed of 1,490 [[Kilometer per hour/Legends|kilometers per hour]].<ref name="RECG" /> It was also equipped with a class 1 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]<ref name="SoT" /> and [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]],<ref name="RECG" /> another unusual feature for a TIE fighter which enabled the TIE phantom to travel between [[Star system/Legends|star systems]].<ref name="SoT" />

===Cloaking device===
[[File:BillyZaneAttacks-FoC.png|thumb|right|250px|A TIE phantom fires its laser cannons.]]
However, the TIE phantom's most unusual feature was its Sienar Fleet Systems [[Mk. III Stygium Cloaking Device]]. The [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]] utilized [[Stygium/Legends|stygium]] [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] in a high-energy [[reactor]]<ref name="SoT" /> to give the fighters an ability unheard of in ships their size in recent decades&mdash;the ability to appear effectively invisible to the naked eye, while at the same time evading [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] and scanners aboard other vessels. When a TIE phantom was cloaked, other vessels could, at best, detect only an unusual sensor anomaly and were unable to get a firm reading,<ref name="RAII" /> while the faint shimmering distortion that was the only visible indication of the fighter's presence was easily missed against the dark backdrop of [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="SoT" /> Even other TIE phantoms were unable to penetrate the cloaking shield.<ref name="RAII" /> However, the cloaking device's high power requirements affected other systems; while the cloaking device was active, the fighter's speed was significantly reduced and the hyperdrive,<ref name="SoR" /> sensors, communications systems and weapons were deactivated.<ref name="SoT" /> To take full advantage of the cloaking device, the vessels had a built-in mechanism that allowed the pilot to fire the fighter's lasers at any time, with the cloaking device being automatically shut off and turned back on after every volley. This allowed them to remain unseen until the moment of firing, thus getting the jump on their enemy, and to be virtually invisible the vast majority of the time, even during a [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]].<ref name="RAII" />

The technology in the TIE phantom was considered a potential threat to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], should it have ever fallen into enemy hands. To prevent this scenario, the designers fitted each fighter with a [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]] that could be activated remotely, so that should one ever be captured, nobody would be able to replicate its technology.<ref name="RAII" /> Due to the complexity of its systems and the high production cost of 365,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], TIE phantoms were only ever produced in limited numbers.<ref name="SoT" />

==Role==
[[File:Cloaked_TIE_Phantom.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A TIE phantom activates its cloaking shield.]]
The TIE phantom's cloaking device allowed the fighters to move through space undetected. This invisibility, combined with the hyperspace capability, allowed them to travel to hostile systems to scout enemy positions ahead of an Imperial invasion. During a battle, they could move unseen around the area and look for vulnerable positions to attack,<ref name="FOC Guide" /> and the device also provided a major advantage during dogfights.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The fighters' independence was boosted by a life support system that allowed the crew to operate independently for [[Standard day/Legends|days]] before needing to return to a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]]<ref name="RECG" /> and their ability to carry consumables to feed the crew for up to two [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]].<ref name="SoT" /> The Empire intended to take full advantage of the fighter's capabilities, planning to use a fleet of the vessels to decimate the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Alliance Fleet]]. For its part, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] quickly realized that the TIE phantom posed a major threat, with the ability to cripple their fleet with near impunity.<ref name="RAII" />

Ultimately, however, the "Phantom Fleet" never survived to lead the planned attack on Alliance forces, and the starfighter's usefulness in large-scale battles remained untested. In the limited action they did see, the ships, which were typically used in small [[Flight group/Legends|flight groups]] rather than full [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]], proved effective in strikes on Rebel patrols, typically moving behind the enemy undetected and quickly eliminating them.<ref name="RAII" /> Due to their high cost, the fighters were only assigned to the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy's]] most capable and trusted pilots.<ref name="SoT" />

==History==
===Development===
{{Quote|As you can see, Lord Vader, the units perform admirably. In fact, I think the whole project has proved quite impressive. Why, in a few years&hellip;''"<br />"''What I see, Admiral Sarn, is yet another one of your endless tests. I will not be impressed until I have, under my command, the full power to crush the Rebel Alliance.|Admiral Sarn and Darth Vader|audio=SarnVader-RAII.flac|<ref name="RAII" />}}
During the reign of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]], ships featuring cloaking devices had been fairly common throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Insider66">{{InsiderCite|66|Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals}}</ref> However, a ban on cloaking technology imposed by the Republic in the decades before the rise of the Galactic Empire,<ref name="SoT" /> combined with the depletion of the stygium crystals [[Mining/Legends|mines]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Aeten II/Legends|Aeten II]] in the [[Dreighton Nebula/Legends|Dreighton Nebula]], saw cloaking devices became increasingly rare,<ref name="Insider66" /> with the [[Scimitar/Legends|Sith Infiltrator]], developed shortly before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]<ref name="NEGVV">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> being among the last known examples of stygium-cloaked vessels.<ref name="NEGVV" />

[[File:ShadowSquadronPilot-XWMG.jpg|thumb|right|250px|TIE phantoms]]
Following the loss of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] at the hands of the Rebel Alliance at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]<ref name="NEC" /> the [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial hierarchy]] sought a weapon that would catch the Rebels off-guard and ensure the Empire's ultimate victory.<ref name="RAII" /> To this end, the Empire began searching through old ship designs in search of anything that might prove useful, and it was this that led Sienar Fleet Systems engineers to uncover plans for a stygium cloaking device that could be fitted to a starfighter or [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]]. Sienar started work on creating a working cloaking device<ref name="SoT" /> and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] charged [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Martio Batch]]&mdash;whose low profile, resulting from his reluctance to engage in [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Court]] [[Politics/Legends|politics]], made him an ideal candidate to lead a secret project&mdash;with overseeing the development.<ref name="Insider66" />

Working out of a [[Imdaar Alpha research station|research station]] on [[Imdaar Alpha]], Batch spent years seeking an alternative to the depleted stygium crystals, developing a system based around [[Hibridium/Legends|hibridium]]. However, the hibridium-based cloaking device suffered from "double blindness," leaving the cloaked vessel blind to its surroundings.<ref name="Insider66" /> Around [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Batch abandoned the hibridium-based cloaking technology and instead devised a way to acquire a new supply of stygium crystals. To this end, he ordered the [[Tarkin (superweapon)|''Tarkin'']] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], a stripped-down version of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], to Aeten II. Batch used the ''Tarkin'' to shatter the planet, releasing millions of stygium crystals from the planet core to be used in his new project.<ref name="NEC" />

With the supply of stygium crystals secured, Batch was soon able to recreate the old cloaking technology.<ref name="Insider66" /> At the facility on Imdaar Alpha, the Empire began fitting modified V38 assault fighters with the technology, with the aim of producing a fleet of the cloaked starfighters. In addition to the stygium, the fighters required a supply of [[oridium]] [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]], and the Empire established a [[Arah mining facility|mining facility]] in the [[Arah asteroid belt|Belt of Arah]] to extract and process the [[Ore/Legends|ore]].<ref name="RAII" /> To protect the development project, Batch requisitioned the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Terror]]'', under the command of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Sarn]].<ref name="Insider66" /> Both the ''Terror'' and the Imdaar Alpha facility were also fitted with the cloaking technology.<ref name="RAII" />

===Testing===
Initial prototypes of the new starfighter were tested near [[Dreighton]], with [[Sigma Squadron (TIE/ph Phantom)|Sigma Squadron]] among the first units of the fighters to become operational. Ever since the [[Battle of Dreighton]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], unexplained events and sightings of ghost ships had been reported in the area of the [[Dreighton Triangle]], and the Empire took advantage of the situation as a cover for their trials.<ref name="RAII" /> An additional squadron of the fighters were assigned to the [[481st Experimental Starfighter Testing Squadron]], under the command of [[Lieutenant Commander/Legends|Lieutenant Commander]] [[Gareth Agamar]].<ref name="SoR" /> The Rebel Alliance became aware that the Empire was working on a major project and dispatched [[Ru Murleen]] to the planet Imdaar to monitor the area. Murleen reported unusually high levels of Imperial activity, though she was unaware of the nature of the threat.<ref name="RAII" />

[[File:Phantoms_in_the_Dark.png|thumb|left|200px|481st phantoms cloak after destroying a target in the Polis Massa system.]]
Based out of the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] [[Mephitis (EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate)|''Mephitis'']], the 481st began conducting trials of the new fighters in the region of [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]], from flying through [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid fields]] to hit-and-run attacks against shipping in the area. Their first target was a two-ship patrol of [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighters]] from the [[88th Attack Squadron]], based out of the Rebel Alliance's [[Polis Massa Research Base]]. This was followed by a series of attacks on Rebel patrols, freighters and nearby [[Archaeologist|archaeological digs]] and research facilities. After [[Black box/Legends|flight recorder]] footage from one of the lost patrols showed a brief glimpse of a TIE phantom, the Rebels stepped up patrols by both the 88th Attack Squadron and [[94th Fighter/Attack Squadron]] in an effort to track down the mysterious attackers. The increase in Rebel patrols made it more difficult for the 481st to act and the squadron began to take losses. The ''Mephitis'' eventually withdrew from the area, putting an end to the testing, but it was clear to the Empire that the Rebels had a larger presence in the region than initially thought.<ref name="SoR" />

Delays to the TIE phantom project caused by mishaps on early trials eventually resulted in the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] arriving at Imdaar Alpha to oversee the final stages of the project. From aboard the ''Terror'', Vader observed a trial in which Sigma Squadron attacked three Rebel [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wings]] on patrol in the Dreighton Triangle. All three X-wings were destroyed, and Sarn considered it a successful demonstration, though he anticipated further time to test the technology. Vader, however, was impatient with the seemingly endless tests. Under the Dark Lord's supervision, the final field tests were soon completed and Vader ordered the full scale production of the new fighters. Before long, a fleet of thousands of the TIE phantoms stood ready at Imdaar Alpha.<ref name="RAII" />

===Rebel intervention===
{{Quote|That's where they're making the phantom TIEs! There must be thousands of them in there. If we don't do something about them, it doesn't matter if we get this thing home or not!''"<br />"''Uh&hellip; what do you have in mind?''"<br />"''Maybe it's better if you don't know. Just hang on and don't let go of those blaster controls.|Ru Murleen and Rookie One|audio=RookieOneMurleen2-RAII.flac|<ref name="RAII" />}}
[[File:TIEPhantomRack-RA2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A rack of TIE phantoms inside the ''Terror''.]]
Rebel agents aboard the YT-1300 light freighter ''[[Corellia Star]]'' provided the Alliance's best lead when they uncovered information about the mining facility in the Belt of Arah supplying fuel for some new Imperial weapon. As the crew attempted to deliver the information to the Alliance Fleet, however, the freighter was captured by Imperial forces and taken to Dreighton. Two Rebel [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wings]] on patrol near Dreighton intercepted the ''Corellia Star''{{'s}} distress signal and moved to investigate. As with the patrol three days earlier, however, they soon came under [[Battle in the Dreighton system|attack]] from the TIE phantoms, the cloaked fighters taking them by surprise, killing the pilot [[Kirby]] and forcing the other, [[Rookie One]], to crash-land on the planet.<ref name="RAII" />

Rookie One was able to escape from Dreighton aboard the ''Corellia Star'' and return to the Alliance Fleet with the information the ship carried. This led Admiral [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] to dispatch [[Rascal Squadron]] on a [[Battle of Arah|mission]] to disable the oridium processing operation in the Belt of Arah. The Rebels successfully destroyed the mining facility, but as they prepared to jump to hyperspace, three TIE phantoms decloaked behind them and successfully eliminated two of the X-wings before they could react. Again, Rookie One managed to survive, jumping to hyperspace moments before the Imperial fighters could destroy his ship.<ref name="RAII" />

[[File:TIEPhantom2.png|thumb|left|250px|Rookie One and Ru Murleen in the cockpit of a TIE phantom.]]
The X-wing's flight recorder showed the capabilities of the TIE phantom. This, together with intelligence showing the ''Terror'' en route to Imdaar, prompted Admiral Ackbar to [[Mission to Imdaar|dispatch]] Rookie One to rendezvous with Ru Murleen on Imdaar. Their mission was to infiltrate the planetary [[Imdaar landing platform|supply platform]], get aboard the ''Terror'', and steal one of the TIE phantoms to be studied by Alliance engineers in the hope of developing a countermeasure. The two Rebel agents successfully boarded the ''Terror'', disguised as [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], as the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] prepared to depart and deploy the fighters against the Alliance. Although the Imperials became alerted to the intruders, the Rebels stole one of the fighters, forcing the Imperials to seal the ''Terror''{{'s}} [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]] to prevent their escape. The Rebels, however, flew the stolen fighter through the network of hangars and into the Super [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer's]] superstructure. As they searched for a way out, they came across the vessel's main reactor, and, realizing that they had the opportunity to destroy the ''Terror'' and the fleet of TIE phantoms that it contained, destroyed the reactor's [[beam focuser]]s, causing it to go critical and explode. As the ''Terror'' began to break up, the Rebels escaped to safety. Darth Vader also escaped the doomed vessel, but not before executing Sarn for his failure.<ref name="RAII" />

[[File:TIE_Phantom_factory.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Rookie One and Ru Murleen approaching the Imdaar Alpha research station aboard a TIE phantom.]]
Though the ''Terror''{{'s}} fate was sealed, the Imperials launched TIE phantoms to prevent the Rebels from escaping to hyperspace. The Imperial fighters forced the stolen ship to turn back toward Imdaar. Despite Rookie One's best efforts, which resulted in the destruction of several of the Imperial fighters, the stolen TIE phantom's deflector shields soon began to fail, though Murleen was able to activate the cloaking device before the Imperials could destroy it. When the ''Terror'' finally blew, the previously cloaked TIE phantom factory on Imdaar Alpha became visible. Murleen quickly realized how many more of the fighters were inside the facility and took the stolen fighter inside. The Rebels destroyed the factory's reactor core, the factory itself, along with the remaining TIE phantoms.<ref name="RAII" />

The stolen TIE phantom was taken back to a Rebel base where the Alliance engineers would examine the technology. Since the Empire had lost its own TIE phantom fleet, the Rebels hoped they could adapt the technology to their own fighters, giving them an advantage in future battles. However, shortly after the vessel docked on the planet, the self-destruct mechanism activated, destroying both the vessel and the technology within it.<ref name="RAII" />

===Aftermath===
{{Quote|The Rebels have eliminated your invincible fleet.''"<br />"''Yes my master, the Rebels have proven surprisingly clever. But we are not defeated.|Emperor Palpatine and Darth Vader|audio=PalpatineVader-RAII.flac|<ref name="RAII" />}}
Following the failure of the TIE phantom project, Batch fled into hiding in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] with his remaining ships to avoid the Emperor's wrath. He was later [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] by his crew, who were still loyal to Admiral Sarn.<ref name="Insider66" /> Only a handful of TIE phantoms remained in service, assigned to the Empire's most capable pilots,<ref name="SoT" /> among them [[Shadow Squadron (TIE Phantom)|Shadow Squadron]].<ref name="FFGXW">{{FFGXW|set=TIE Phantom Expansion Pack|cardname=Shadow Squadron Pilot}}</ref> The Rebel Alliance were unable to locate where the fighters were stationed, but ultimately determined that they no longer posed an immediate threat.<ref name="SoT" /> Though the TIE phantom's technology was lost forever with the destruction of the Imdaar Alpha facility,<ref name="RAII" /> the hibridium technology that preceded it continued to be developed as part of the [[Vorknkx Project]], resulting in a cloaking device being fitted to the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[Vorknkx]]''. Grand Admiral [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] would later use the hibridium cloak to great effect in his [[Thrawn campaign|campaign]] against the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="Insider66" /><ref name="NEC" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|There was one sketch in one of the Star Wars art books that I used as sort of a basis for it. It was actually an early design for the Imperial shuttle. It had this ball front end with this long body, almost like a dragonfly, and then these wings that came up and hung way out over the front. And I thought it worked for this.|Rich Green, on the origin of the TIE phantom design|<ref name="RAII:OPG">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault II Official Player's Guide]]''</ref>}}
[[File:TIEPhantomWireframe.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A TIE phantom]]
The TIE phantom was created by [[Vincent Lee|Vince Lee]] for the [[1995]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire]]''. The fighter was designed by [[Richard Green (artist)|Rich Green]], and based on an early sketch of the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]]. Green adapted the design to make it fit the look of other TIE series fighters, altering the [[Window/Legends|window]] pattern on the cockpit and adding the standard solar panel appearance to the wings. As he refined the idea, Green incorporated suggestions from Lee, including adding scoops to resemble air vents. Green considered the TIE phantom the hardest element of the game to design, making it feel both new, yet instantly recognizable as a TIE series fighter, and also both slick and scary in appearance.<ref name="RAII:OPG" />

Although many fans, including [[Curtis Saxton]] on the [[Curtis Saxton|Star Wars Technical Commentaries]], already called the ship the TIE Phantom,<ref name="SWTC">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/swtc/tie.html|text=STAR WARS: TIE Fighters|author=[[Curtis Saxton]]|work=[[Curtis Saxton|Star Wars Technical Commentaries]]|archivedate=20021203203304}}</ref><ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/6022798|board=Videogames|thread=What is your favourite Imperial starfighter?|user=CrixMakin|date=2002-03-13|time=6:01 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318133100/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/what-is-your-favourite-imperial-starfighter.5958028/page-2#post-6022798}}</ref><ref name="SW forum">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=36969&start=29#927816|thread=The Underused Snubfighters Thread. Woo, Scary.|user=Kaelis|date=2002-04-20|time=8:45 AM}}</ref><ref>[[Special:PermanentLink/13872|TIE Phantom]] on [[Wookieepedia]] (posted [[May 24]], [[2005]] 22:22)</ref> it was not identified as such in a [[canon]] source until the release of ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' in late [[2006]],<ref name="FOC" /> having been previously called only the "Phantom TIE."<ref name="RAII" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="NEGVV" /><ref name="EC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> The fighter was included as a unit type in ''Forces of Corruption'' itself, though the game adds no canonical information about its usage.<ref name="FOC" /> The [[2014]] [[Fantasy Flight Games]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] sourcebook [[Stay on Target (sourcebook)|''Stay on Target'']] later introduced the designation "TIE/ph phantom".<ref name="SoT" />

Though all five of the TIE phantom's laser cannons were clearly visible in ''Rebel Assault II'', only the two under the cockpit were actually shown firing in the game.<ref name="RAII" /> The purpose of the wing-mounted cannons was not confirmed until the release of ''Forces of Corruption'', which showed the fighters making use of all five cannons.<ref name="FOC" /> The [[2009]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] roleplaying sourcebook ''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]'' established that the TIE phantom was equipped with a class 6 hyperdrive; ''Stay on Target'' later amended this to a faster class 1 drive. Likewise, ''Stay on Target'' increased maximum consumables to two weeks from the three days previously given in ''Rebellion Era Campaign Guide''.<ref name="SoT" /><ref name="RECG" />
